title: Cohort-specific fidelity, prompt cropping, and progressive rollback criteria for Optimize
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Purpose: Define a production-ready set of evaluation requirements and acceptance criteria for Redwood Optimize that (1) allow per-cohort fidelity tracking, (2) enable prompt-set cropping to remove noisy prompts during canaries, and (3) specify progressive rollback / failover thresholds for A/B and canary rollouts. This PRD ties product acceptance to concrete statistical tests, minimum sample sizes, and automated failover actions so platform teams can safely promote optimizer recommendations and model/quantization changes.
background: We currently run Optimize evaluations that surface model/quantization recommendations and prompt-level regressions. Past incidents show two recurring failure modes: (a) regressions concentrated in specific user cohorts (e.g., long-form vs. transactional prompts) that are averaged out by global signals, and (b) noisy prompts that cause spurious alerts during short canaries. Engineering needs deterministic guarding logic to support fast rollouts while avoiding both false positives and missed cohort regressions.
scope: In scope: - Define cohort taxonomy for Optimize (length buckets, domain buckets, latency-sensitive vs. throughput-sensitive). - Specify statistical tests (metrics, thresholds, one/two-sided tests) and minimum sample sizes per cohort. - Define prompt cropping heuristics for canaries (how to identify and exclude 'noisy' prompts). - Define progressive rollback actions mapped to signal severity and cohort impact. - Automate gating in the Optimize rollout pipeline and expose human-readable decision artifacts in Console. Out of scope: model training changes, global A/B platform re-architecture, per-customer custom cohort definitions (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Cohort taxonomy defined and documented: length buckets (<64, 64-512, 512-2048, >2048), domain tags (support, creative, code, search), and SLA categories (latency-sensitive vs. throughput-first)

For each cohort, minimum effective sample size computed and enforced during canary: at least 200 completed prompts per cohort OR statistical power >= 0.8 for detecting a 3% absolute drop in primary quality metric

Primary/secondary signals defined: primary = composite quality score (composed of relevance, factuality, and human-rated helpfulness proxies), secondary = latency, token-usage delta, and hallucination indicator

Statistical tests specified: two-sided bootstrap CI for composite quality, Benjamini-Hochberg correction for per-prompt multiple comparisons, and pre-registered one-sided threshold for latency regressions

Prompt cropping rules implemented: prompts with >20% outlier loss vs. cohort median or >3 standard deviations in response-length divergence marked as noisy and excluded from short canaries; cropped prompt lists are recorded and surfaced in Console

Progressive rollback policy documented and implemented: soft-fail (pause new traffic) at cohort-level degradation >= 1.5x detection threshold, full rollback at degradation >= 3x threshold OR when two or more adjacent cohorts exceed medium impact thresholds

A/B decision matrix implemented: - If global composite quality delta > 1.5% and cohort deltas aligned, full rollout allowed. - If global delta < 1.5% but at least one cohort shows high-impact regression, trigger per-cohort failover and block global promotion
Automated flags and human escalation: alerts posted to oncall channel, incident playbook link included, and a single-click rollback button in Console that triggers safe rollback within SLA
End-to-end test harness: synthetic canary run that intentionally injects a known regression and verifies the pipeline pauses/rolls back according to the policy
Documentation and runbook updated in Confluence with examples and explanation of statistical choices
success_metrics: Reduction in missed cohort regressions (measured by post-release incident counts) by >= 60% over baseline
False positive rollback rate under 5% for canaries running standard sample sizes
Mean time to rollback <= 10 minutes when automated conditions are met
Increase in confidence score (internal metric) for Optimize recommendations by 20% among platform users
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (spike/prototype): 2-week spike to implement cohort tagging and sample-size calculator in dev environment; validate on historical evals
Phase 1 (canary): run with prompt-cropping enabled for 4 weeks on 5% of Optimize traffic; monitor false-positive rate and hand-curate crop heuristics
Phase 2 (progressive rollout): expand to 25% traffic with automated per-cohort pause; run dual outputs (old/new) for 1 week
Phase 3 (full enable): universal enforcement across Optimize runs and expose controls in Console; deprecate temporary experiment flags after 2 release cycles
Rollback/Failover steps: automated soft-fail (holdback new requests) -> immediate alert + owner notification -> single-click rollback (revert model/quant config) -> postmortem and prompt-set audit
test_plan: Unit tests for sample-size calculator and cohort assignment logic
Integration test that simulates per-cohort degradation and verifies automated pause and rollback triggers
End-to-end test that validates prompt-cropping preserves statistical validity (no greater than 2% bias introduced)
A/B test harness updates to record per-prompt exclusion reasons and surface counts in experiment dashboard
risks: Overly aggressive prompt-cropping could bias canary results and mask real regressions
Insufficient sample sizes in low-traffic cohorts may produce noisy signals and unnecessary rollbacks
Complexity of per-cohort policies increases cognitive load for SRE and oncall teams
False sense of safety if composite score weighting misrepresents user-perceived quality
open_questions: What is the canonical list of domain tags we should support out of the box? (support, creative, code, search, summarization, classification)
Should per-customer custom cohorts be supported in phase 2 or deferred to a later effort?
What is the recommended composite quality weighting between relevance, factuality proxies, and human-label proxies?
Edge case: how to handle cohorts with rapidly changing distributions (e.g., seasonal spikes) — auto-increase sample-size or flag as unstable?
notes: PM will run two stakeholder workshops: (1) stats review with Applied ML to validate thresholds and multiple-testing approach, (2) SRE workshop to finalize failover choreography. Expect a small follow-up PRD to cover per-customer cohort customizations.
post_release_actions: Quarterly audit of cropped prompts and per-cohort regression incidents; feed audit results into prompt-set pruning recommendations for Optimize
